On XXX, X wrote:
> Hello!
>
> I am using your R package "BioGeoBEARS" in R studio and I have tried to run it for several hours and have been unsuccessful. The error code I keep receiving is:

> FATAL ERROR in inputs: 1 tree tips are not in the geographic ranges file.  These are:

>
> I am not sure what this means, but I have spent hours trying to figure it out. I have attached my tree and geography spread, as well as the text file.
>
> Any help you can provide is awesome and would be much appreciated!
>
> Thanks,
> XXXX
>

---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Nick Matzke <mat...@nimbios.org>
Date: Sat, Mar 5, 2016 at 3:50 PM
Subject: Re: Error in BioGeoBEARS
To: XXXX

Hi XXXX,

So, your geography file has a list of species, and your newick file has a list of species.  These lists have to match *exactly*.  The error message is saying that you are missing a species in your geography file.

Cheers!
Nick

That's the right idea, but keep in mind that the first state is the null range (living in null areas).  If you mean to exclude the null range from the state space, that's fine, but it should be done by setting BioGeoBEARS_run_object$include_null_range = FALSE, since all sorts of annoyingly special things happen in internally in the code, related to the null range.

Once you've excluded the null range, you would exclude the other states accordingly (making sure you count the indexes correctly; they will all be shifted one).  See how to get the list of states here:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#node_probabilities

For discussion of what happens when you exclude the null range, see Massana et al. on bioarxiv, the title is something like Non-null effects of null range.

A little more discussion of modifying the state space manually:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/biogeobears/areas_allowed/biogeobears/8UQB_RI_ohQ/R7qJAdh4CQAJ
===================
You can manually edit the states_list, however, to set up whatever list of allowed states you like. This would be done in the R script and not in a text file. See various discussions on the BioGeoBEARS google group, e.g.
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/biogeobears/areas_allowed$20adjacency/biogeobears/7e7U9NtPTBU/pnNtR9M7migJ
===================

Cheers,
Nick

messages.body_plain:
Hi Nick,

I tried to fix the state of some nodes in a time-stratified analysis but BioGeoBEARS could not calculate a likelihood (see the example below).

I modified calc_loglike_sp_stratified.R to enable this kind of analysis (see attachment). Unfortunately, I used an old script. I haven't visited this google group for a while and I missed your update of the new source files <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/biogeobears/eqyPITabhQw> (Not sure whether I will need the the trait option but looks cool!). Nevertheless, my modified script and the newly sourced files works together in this case (see also below).

My old script <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/biogeobears/Torsten/biogeobears/7bBNhV904f8/cJMUW_v9AAAJ> of calc_loglike_sp_stratified.R seems to be a bit shorter than your recent version but includes the lists_of_states_lists_0based feature.

However, I modified four lines only (changes in red and line numbers according to your recent version of calc_loglike_sp_stratified.R):
L781: temporary_fixlikes = fixlikes[fixnodes_in_subtree_TF, states_allowed_TF]
L870: tmp_fixlikes = temporary_fixlikes[states_allowed_TF]
L2656: (length(tmp_fixnode) > 1)
L2674: tmp_relprobs_at_branchtop_AT_node_UPPASS[anc,] =  tmp_relprobs_at_branchtop_AT_node_UPPASS[anc,] * temporary_fixlikes[states_allowed_TF]

Cheers,
Torsten

messages.body_plain:
P.S.: Another way to fix the states at certain nodes would be to insert direct ancestors (tips with length < 0.0000001) very close to a particular node. This is simpler in some ways.  On the other hand, it "changes the data" (different input file of the tip ranges), so might not be as ideal for using e.g. AIC to compare different fixed states decisions. On the other, other, hand, the results would be directly comparable if any direct ancestor tips that you don't want to use in a particular model were given likelihood 1 for all states -- this would require manually specifying the tip conditional likelihoods for each tip.

Cheers!
Nick

Hi Nick,

I've attached the files. A bit of background in case this helps; I've performed the dating analysis in MrBayes so the tree is ultrametric but the actual node ages are stored in a separate output file i.e. the branch lengths will look like they are scaled in substitutions. There are some polytomies which I resolved using multi2di(my.tree, random=TRUE) and I've given the new branch lengths a very short length that is still longer than the min_branchlength that would cause BioGeoBEARS to interpret them as a hook. The following code chunk will get you from the attached tree to the tree that fails to plot.

### read in the resolved tree
tree.resolve<-read.nexus("resolved_tree.nex")

### give zero length branches an arbitrarily short length that is higher than the min branch length for BioGeoBEARS
### this prevents BioGeoBEARS from interpreting the ultra short branch as a direct ancestor.
tree.resolve$edge.length<-ifelse(tree.resolve$edge.length==0,0.00001,tree.resolve$edge.length)

Many Thanks,

James

I've always felt a little unsure of MCC trees simply because I think a polytomy is a more obvious way of showing the uncertainty in your data (or it may even be real i.e. speciation at time scales below the resolution of your dataset) but I guess for a biogeographic analysis, why not show the most credible scenario across the sampled trees?

Many Thanks for pointing out the formatting errors.

James

The BEAST MCC trees make more sense to me, being one of the sampled tree topologies which are fully resolved...

messages.body_plain:
I wanted to add to this thread for future users. I came up with the same fatal error while trying to check inputs using

check_BioGeoBEARS_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)

I discovered that the error was caused by an extra white space that was included in the species names in the species range file (geogfn). That file was created in excel, saved as a tab delimited text file and then modified the file using RegEx in Notepad++. However, I did not realize that each name was followed by a space, followed by a tab, followed by the range data. After removing the space (keeping only the single tab) everything ran smoothly.

Thanks for your question.  There is no simple solution here, but loose thoughts:

- You should edit the pdf() command in the script to shrink the tiplabels and/or make the PDF taller; some version of this may look "good enough"

- Because there are so many states (all the different ranges, often hundreds), and the human eye can only effectively read 10 or so colors on a chart, colors in general have limits, and these get worse for thin lines rather than boxes/pies.

- You could pick some cutoff, but any cutoff would be arbitrary, and anyway it would take a bunch of extra calculations and programming to figure out when a branch switched from 49% B to 50% B, or whatever.  Probabilities are calculated at the nodes in phylogenetic models (and at corners, in BioGeoBEARS biogeography models) purely because that is convenient and efficient. In reality, every point on every branch could have probabilities calculated for it, and probabilities will change smoothly along the branches

- Even if you did decide on/program a solution, depicting the majority or plurality vote at various points on the tree is itself an approximation that is sometimes misleading:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-mistakes-to-avoid#Most_prob_states_not_joint

- It would be much simpler to just do Biogeographical Stochastic Mapping, and then present one or a few of these histories, or present one and then have a sample of 50 in a PDF in the Supp. Mat.  This is also the One True Way to count events:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-mistakes-to-avoid#Most_prob_states_not_events

Cheers!
Nick
